name: Level_1 - Task_10
description: Evaluate the 2D in-plane mechanical stiffness of graphene. Construct a primitive graphene unit cell containing two carbon atoms (lattice parameter a = 2.46 Å) with 15 Å of vacuum padding along the z-axis. The MACE-MP-0 foundation model should be used as the ASE-compatible calculator to describe interatomic interactions. Perform a constrained geometric relaxation of the system using the BFGS optimizer until the maximum atomic force falls below 0.005 eV/Å. During this optimization, allow the internal atomic positions and the in-plane cell vectors to fully relax, but strictly constrain the out-of-plane cell dimension and cross-plane shear components. After relaxation, calculate the equilibrium in-plane cell area, A₀ = |a₁ × a₂|. Generate 11 biaxially strained configurations by uniformly scaling the relaxed in-plane lattice vectors by factors ranging from 0.98 to 1.02. Scale the atomic coordinates proportionally in the xy-plane without altering the out-of-plane vacuum layer. Compute the single-point potential energy for each strained configuration without performing any further structural relaxation. Fit the resulting energy-area data to a quadratic polynomial ($E(A) = aA^2 + bA + c$) and compute the 2D in-plane stiffness using the relation K_2D = 2aA₀. Convert the final result from eV/Å² to N/m (using the conversion factor 1 eV/Å² = 16.0217662 N/m) and return it as a floating-point value.
